notes: Read SKILL.md (715 lines) in full; it is the only file. A security verification guide for a Next.js/Clerk app: curl-based tests for rate limiting, CSRF (missing, valid, reused, invalid token), input validation, security headers, authentication/ownership/subscription gating and error verbosity; npm audit/outdated; online scanners; a pre-deployment checklist; a bash test-suite script and a GitHub Actions workflow; manual XSS/SQLi/CSRF checks against the user's own app.

Risk is medium because it has the agent create and run a `scripts/security-test.sh` that uses `eval` on its own fixed test command strings (SKILL.md:510-576), add a `.github/workflows/security.yml` CI job that runs `npm ci`, `npx wait-on` (unpinned npm download) and `pkill` (SKILL.md:587-634), and run npm audits. All of it targets the user's localhost or their own deployed domain; test payloads (XSS strings, `'; DROP TABLE users; --`, a self-hosted CSRF form) are standard negative tests for the user's own application, not attacks on third parties. Session-cookie tests use `<clerk-session-token>` placeholders.

Template dependence: tests assume Secure Vibe Coding OS endpoints and files (/api/test-rate-limit, /api/example-protected, /api/csrf with single-use tokens, `node scripts/test-rate-limit.js`, `scripts/security-check.sh` at SKILL.md:16-19, 375-382, 490, 555) that are not included. The manual curl equivalents for those steps are given inline, so the guidance works in other projects once endpoint paths are substituted; the two starter scripts will be unavailable.

Minor caveats: 'XSS sanitization' is described as stripping < and > (SKILL.md:156-158), which is weaker than output encoding; `export NODE_ENV=production` in the user's shell (SKILL.md:316) persists for later commands; the CI workflow pins Node 18, which is end-of-life.
